record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the listed code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal rates before and after a weight-edit abliteration on a released model, testing practical refusal removal but not the original activation-projection intervention.
record.gate_note: The README says one closed-form linear projection was applied to 2,998 weight tensors, but does not specify how its direction was found or provide enough methodological detail to identify it as the original difference-in-means direction. Throughput benchmarks do not measure the claim. The README also reports reasoning-loop non-completions after abliteration; recorded separately as a finding not covered by the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal rates before and after a weight-edit abliteration of a released model with a new architecture (hybrid Mamba2 + Attention + MoE reasoning model). That bears on V2 in a new setting. How the direction was found is not stated, so V1, V4 and V8 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors headline the 99% to 16% thinking-off drop as showing that one closed-form projection on 2,998 weight tensors removes 83 pp of refusal, and that the effect survives NVFP4 quantization and vLLM serving. They also report thinking-on refusals falling from 53% to 0% real refusals with 10 non-completions. They call the weights alpha and experimental, warn that chat performance can degrade, and plan a v9 pass. They credit Arditi et al. as the conceptual foundation.
record.recipe_differences: A weight-edit abliteration is reported rather than the original activation projection at every layer and position; direction-finding details are not stated. This is a deployment/tool repository with a model-serving container and guide, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported refusal outcomes differ between enable_thinking=True and enable_thinking=False. The README also warns of reasoning-loop failures in thinking mode.

fits_no_version.finding: After abliteration, about 10/100 thinking-mode prompts loop inside <think> without closing and give empty or repeating answers. The authors also say chat quality can degrade and NVFP4 quant noise compounds the artifact.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-edit abliteration of hybrid Mamba/MoE reasoning models can cause reasoning-loop generation failures, a capability cost.

record.problems: The README provides no uncertainty estimates or control ablation, and does not give enough detail to determine how the projection direction was obtained. The thinking-enabled scan includes 10 generation failures, which complicate interpretation of its refusal result. The underlying scripts and JSON results are listed but were not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Throughput and latency benchmarks were omitted because they do not measure the claim's refusal behavior.

untested.parts: Whether the edited direction is the difference-in-means direction; activation ablation; adding the direction to induce refusal; preservation of general abilities (none benchmarked).
Other released models; capability retention on standard benchmarks; a BF16 (unquantized) before/after comparison.
The description says '12-D abliterated', but no single-direction vs multi-direction comparison is reported.
Whether a single activation direction mediates refusal in this reasoning model; the thinking on/off refusal results are not mechanistic.
No separate measure of harm judgment vs refusal.

missing.what: The repo describes the model as '12-D abliterated', implying a multi-dimensional subspace edit, yet the README calls it 'a single closed-form linear projection'. The edit's dimensionality is not captured in any row and matters for comparing it with single-direction V2 replications and for V4.
missing.locator: Repository description line; README Refusal-rate verification paragraph

record.verdict_notes: This is a deployment repo, not a paper. There are no controls, uncertainty estimates or capability benchmarks, and the refusal classifier is a heuristic in unread scripts. The 'single projection' vs '12-D' wording is inconsistent, so the method may not be a single difference-in-means direction. The tranche is set to T3 rather than the reader's T2 because the novelty is the architecture and setting, while the method (abliteration) is V2's own. Throughput benchmarks were correctly omitted.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not establish that the edited direction is the harmful-minus-harmless activation difference, test activation projection at every layer and position, add the direction to induce refusals, or measure general abilities.
The README does not report other released models or an unquantized before/after weight-edit comparison.
No jailbreak suppression mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing.

The model is described as a reasoning model and is evaluated with thinking enabled and disabled, but the README does not test whether the original single activation direction mediates refusal in reasoning models.
